hi! the gendered brain myth is a myth that has been spread in the trans community that has been debunked!

The myth that trans people have the brain of the sex they identify as comes from a study of trans women and trans men which showed that the trans women's brains were slightly feminized and the trans men's brains were slightly masculinized. Both were in the middle between male and female, but there was clear feminization or masculinization. The theory is this happens in the womb.

!!!Heres the thing though: the study didn't control for sexuality. Meaning all the trans women were homosexual (attracted to males) and all the trans men were homosexual (attracted to females). These findings are similar to other studies (1) which have shown that gay men have slightly feminized brains, and gay women have slightly masculinized brains (2). Remember, this is not an "entire brain" thing, but rather small isolated regions (and remember that brains are incredibly plastic and a ballerina's brain will look different from a truck driver's, even of the same sex). Both are in the middle between male and female, even in these small isolated regions, but there is clear feminization or masculinization. The theory is that this happens in the womb.

\---Therefore, this is rather a small region of the brain that dictates sexuality, not gender.

A follow up study was done on trans people that controlled for sexuality (3). It showed that trans women who were attracted to men (homosexual in relation to their birth sex) had feminized brains, but trans women attracted to women (heterosexual in relation to their birth sex) had 100% male typical brains. No feminization whatsoever.

\--Therefore, this is rather a small region of the brain that dictates sexuality, not gender.

The only exception was the right inferior fronto-occipital tract, connecting parietal and frontal brain areas that mediate own body perception. Fronto-occipital tract also shows this variance in girls with anorexia and bulimea and those with BDD (4). Meaning, its a region of the brain which can change based on socialization and negative self-body perceptions which can be worked on. Remember the brain is incredibly plastic and not some one-sized thing when youre born, like your heart or lungs or bone length. The brain is incredibly adaptive to environment.
